name: 20000-leagues-translations
work: Jules Verne, Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea(s) (Vingt mille lieues sous les mers, 1870)
description: Two competing English TRANSLATIONS of the same French novel — the material 'variant English editions of Verne' actually means (English Verne is always a translation of the French original). base = the older Mercier translation. The Part 1, Chapter 1 excerpts (mercier.txt / walter.txt) are the routine collation-test witnesses; the whole-novel witnesses (full/mercier.txt, full/walter.txt) are for scale/benchmark testing.

mercier.translation: Lewis Page Mercier ('Mercier Lewis'), the Sampson Low, 1872 'standard' English translation — known for abridging and altering the French
mercier.excerpt: Part 1, Chapter I 'A Shifting Reef' (between '^CHAPTER I$' and '^CHAPTER II$')

walter.translation: Frederick Paul Walter, a modern faithful/unabridged English translation

notes: The excerpt pair yields ~403 variants (heavy substitution + transposition + edits-within-moves) — a demanding real-world substantive-variation test, the same kind as conformance case 20-verne-translation but a full chapter. The WHOLE-NOVEL witnesses under full/ collate in ~3 s (~21.8k variants) and are the engine's largest real scale test; they exposed and now guard against an inverted-range crash (fixed 2026-07-01, see ../known-issues/README.md).
